coverage: Nine stories · AI coding, teen social media, digital habits, creator tools, outages, satellites and Seattle space computing

cards.headline: GPT-6.1 Sol targets harder coding with fewer resources
cards.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Sol for ChatGPT Work and Codex, saying its tests show stronger coding, computer-use and professional-work performance than GPT-6 Sol. GitHub also began rolling the model into Copilot for agentic coding and terminal workflows.
cards.whyItMatters: AI coding tools are becoming more capable, but their benchmark scores are vendor tests rather than guarantees. Programmers still need to review generated code and verify results.

csp.connection: AI coding agents can generate and modify programs, while humans test whether the output actually meets requirements.

cards.headline: Instagram adds verified school spaces for high-school students
cards.summary: Meta expanded Instagram's School Partnership Program with school Channels, Stories and Notes plus student Clubs & Teams and a school directory. High-school students must pass third-party verification to enter a verified school community, and participating schools can moderate school-related content.
cards.whyItMatters: A social app is adding digital identity checks and school-controlled spaces. That creates a useful example of how platforms balance communication, verification, privacy and moderation.

csp.connection: Online communities depend on design choices about identity, access, moderation and who can see shared information.

cards.headline: Apple and pediatricians publish a family screen-time guide
cards.summary: Apple and the American Academy of Pediatrics released guidance that pairs healthy digital-habit advice with Apple's parental controls. It covers conversations about screen time, age-based safeguards, app and website approval, schedules and communication settings.
cards.whyItMatters: Technology design can shape sleep, schoolwork, exercise and social time. Controls such as schedules and permissions are examples of software turning family rules into system behavior.

csp.connection: Computing products affect daily behavior, and designers can build controls that give users and families more choices.

cards.headline: Creator apps add smarter editing and collaboration tools
cards.summary: Apple announced Creator Studio updates including finer image-selection controls in Pixelmator Pro, editable Cinematic effects in Final Cut Pro and new collaboration features. Keynote can also generate images for slides, while Freeform can use Apple Intelligence to rewrite or summarize handwritten notes.
cards.whyItMatters: Creative software combines algorithms with human choices rather than replacing the creator. Selection masks, generated images and shared documents all turn different kinds of data into editable media.

csp.connection: Digital creators use software tools iteratively to produce, revise and share computing artifacts.

cards.headline: iPhone camera app exposes more pro video controls
cards.summary: Final Cut Camera 2.4 adds variable-aperture control for iPhone 18 Pro plus redesigned controls for exposure, focus and recording. With iOS 27 it can also show RGB color-channel data and histograms, tools filmmakers use to judge color balance and brightness.
cards.whyItMatters: A phone camera is a sensor system that turns light into numerical image data. Professional controls expose more of that pipeline instead of hiding every decision behind automatic processing.

csp.connection: Digital cameras sample physical light into data that software can measure, transform, display and store.

cards.headline: Spotify and Claude recover from separate service outages
cards.summary: Spotify and Anthropic's Claude both experienced brief U.S. service disruptions Tuesday, according to Reuters and user reports collected by Downdetector. Anthropic said its Claude issues were mitigated, while Spotify acknowledged problems and investigated them.
cards.whyItMatters: Apps that feel local often depend on remote servers and networks. When a cloud service fails, thousands of users can notice at once even though their own phones and computers are working.

csp.connection: Internet services rely on connected servers, networks and software layers, so failures can affect many clients at the same time.

cards.headline: Landsat 9 marks five years of mapping Earth
cards.summary: NASA says Landsat 9 completed its five-year design life after collecting science-grade images of Earth's surface since 2021. Paired with Landsat 8, the satellites provide near-weekly observations used for agriculture, disasters, forests, fires, water and environmental research.
cards.whyItMatters: Satellite images become large datasets that computers can compare across years. Open Earth-observation data lets researchers detect patterns and changes that would be difficult to measure from the ground.

csp.connection: Computing systems collect, store and analyze repeated measurements to reveal changes across large places and long periods.

cards.headline: UW students invite new Huskies to code physics for space
cards.summary: The University of Washington's Husky Satellite Lab held a Seattle workshop where students could build ray-tracing algorithms that simulate light through Earth's atmosphere. The lab highlighted computer vision, star tracking, orbital simulation and other algorithms it wants to test with satellite cameras.
cards.whyItMatters: This is computing happening close to home and beyond Earth. The same ideas students learn about algorithms and simulation can become tools for spacecraft navigation and scientific research.

csp.connection: A simulation is a program that uses algorithms and mathematical models to represent behavior in the physical world.

cards.headline: UW workshop asks what a satellite computer really needs
cards.summary: Husky Satellite Lab also challenged students to design a miniature flight computer while considering radiation, limited power, lost connections, processors, storage and sensors. The exercise showed why spacecraft computers face constraints that ordinary laptops do not.
cards.whyItMatters: Computer design is about tradeoffs, not simply choosing the fastest chip. Engineers match hardware and software to the environment, reliability needs, power budget and data a system must handle.

csp.connection: A computing system's hardware, storage, sensors and communication links must work together under real-world constraints.
